$comment: The allowlist. Nothing is downloaded that is not named here, and there is
no crawling: the fetcher reads this list and fetches exactly these URLs.
Every entry below is a fact, not a proposal. The names come from the
renderer's own layer templates, which are public:
https://www.hearthcards.net/assets_template_new/minion.json
https://www.hearthcards.net/assets_template_new/spell.json
https://www.hearthcards.net/assets_template_new/heropower.json
The hero power template's own Type id is 'heropower', not 'power' - the
obvious guess resolves to the site's index page at HTTP 200, exactly the
trap described below. It was found by reading the app's own bundled
script for the literal string it fetches (fetch(`/assets_template_new/
${Type}.json`)) rather than guessed a second time.
The first version of this file was guessed from one known URL and a
supposed naming rule. Twelve of fifteen names were wrong, and the site
answers an unknown path with its own index page at HTTP 200, so every
wrong guess looked like a success. Hence the rule now: a name is in this
file because the renderer references it, never because it seems plausible.
'sourceRect' is where the renderer draws that component on the 800x1100
canvas. It is recorded because it is a fact worth keeping, not because
anything reads it yet: our recipe carries its own rects.
Each entry also says where the file belongs on one of our cards, so
filling the catalog is reading this file rather than wiring anything by
hand. Adding a component is adding an entry - no new code.
The renderer composes on 800 x 1100, which is the canvas this project
has used since its card layout was first measured. Components are not
full-canvas layers: each is its own small image placed at its own rect,
which is exactly how our painter draws them.
The minion art window is an ellipse. The renderer offers both an
ellipse and a rectangle mask for it, and our recipe currently uses the
rectangle - the same 186,185 434x420 the template lists.
The renderer's full class table, recorded as a fact and deliberately
not turned into entries. Our engine's CardClass has only Neutral, so an
entry naming any of these would be a mapping to a value that does not
exist. When a class is added to CardClass, its two lines move down into
'entries' and nothing else changes.
Note the two different words for the same idea: a minion frame is
Card_Inhand_Minion_<Class>, and a spell frame is
Card_Inhand_Ability_<Class>. No rule derives the second from the first.
This is the single reason the guessed manifest could never have worked.

entries.purpose: The hero power frame. Its own art window is an ellipse near the card's centre (267,269 270x269), which is why this medallion is round rather than a shape approximated in code. Unlike the minion, spell and hero frames, the renderer's own template draws this one layer as type 'static' rather than 'classMapping' - one file for every class, 'Neutral' in the name notwithstanding - so this entry is deliberately left unconstrained by class rather than copying the per-class convention its siblings use for a real reason.

$comment: Real components the renderer uses that our composer has no slot for. They
are recorded so the next person does not have to discover them again, and
left out of 'entries' so nothing downloads a file with nowhere to put it.
There is no card back among them: the renderer draws card fronts, so our
own back stays scaffolding until somebody draws one.
